name: MATHVISTA
description: A benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA), covering diverse mathematical reasoning types, tasks, and visual contexts.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
citeAs: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao. MATHVISTA: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024.
rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA was compiled from 31 source datasets: 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA). The authors collected 9 existing MathQA datasets in multimodal settings, reviewed more than 70 VQA datasets and selected 19 publicly available datasets containing math-related instances, and created 3 new datasets to address gaps in logical reasoning on puzzle test diagrams, algebraic reasoning on function plots, and scientific reasoning on academic figures. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were first used to automatically select likely math-related examples, followed by manual labeling by three expert annotators to determine whether examples involved mathematical reasoning. For the three new datasets, questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Others
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset is derived from 31 source datasets, including 9 existing MathQA datasets, 19 publicly available VQA datasets containing math-related instances, and 3 newly annotated datasets: IQTest sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms, FunctionQA, and PaperQA with 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface. Academic illustrations were taken from online education resources, including tables, figures, and charts.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA examples were sourced from papers released in August 2023. Multimodal Bard evaluation dates range from Sep 8, 2023 to Sep 10, 2023. GPT-4V evaluation dates range from Oct 7, 2023 to Oct 15, 2023.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation in the final benchmark. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules automatically selected examples with numeric answers or quantity words in the questions, then three expert annotators manually labeled whether they involved mathematical reasoning, and majority voting was used to finalize examples. For release, the dataset was split into testmini and test; testmini was sampled by first randomly sampling questions with a threshold number of 4 for each source dataset and then randomly sampling remaining questions based on source proportion in the entire set.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets not originally math-targeted, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates. Examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words were selected. This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples, after which false positives were removed through manual labeling by expert annotators. The authors also conducted several quality checks to address unidentified errors. Answers were normalized to required answer formats for evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples were annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, visual context, and required reasoning skills. Coarse labels of mathematical reasoning were automatically obtained from source dataset details. To verify automatic annotation quality, expert annotators manually labeled mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples from seven candidates. For the 4,949 filtered VQA examples, three expert annotators manually labeled whether each involved mathematical reasoning, using majority voting. For the three new datasets, all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields, with each dataset independently annotated by three reviewers and disagreements resolved through discussion among the entire review team.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A custom annotation tool with GUI developed by the authors
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the newly collected 736 questions, independent annotation by three reviewers resulted in an inter-annotation consistency rate of 99.2%, with only 6 disagreements resolved through team discussion. For labeling whether problems involved mathematical reasoning, inter-annotator agreement among three annotators was measured with Fleiss Kappa = 0.775, indicating substantial consistency. For mathematical reasoning category verification, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations had the exact same set of reasoning types, while 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three expert annotators were used for manual labeling of mathematical reasoning in VQA examples. Newly collected questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and independently reviewed by three reviewers. Human performance baseline annotators on Amazon Mechanical Turk were required to have a satisfactory annotating history, complete more than 5,000 HIT tasks, have an acceptance score higher than 0.99, pass qualification examples, and possess a high school diploma or higher.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: MATHVISTA is divided into testmini and test. The answer labels for test will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination, and the authors will maintain an online evaluation platform. The benchmark is part of an ongoing research process, and the authors are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Language; grade level; educational attainment of human annotators
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to facilitate development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios and evaluate progress of LLMs and LMMs, with potential applications in educational disciplines, logical queries about statistical data, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. The paper states that MATHVISTA will play a critical role in the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks.
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes dataset coverage limitations, including possible gaps in representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. It also notes that annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in heterogeneous annotations lacking a unified format and structure. For few-shot experiments, the paper notes models may be sensitive to bias in demonstrations. The paper also discusses hallucinations as a major source of errors in generative foundation models and notes potential data noise to be refined.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark may have gaps in representation of certain mathematical problems and visuals. Its focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts spanning domains like science and college-level math requires a labor-intensive collection process, raising concerns about scalability and generalizability to other domains. Only 85.6% of examples have annotations, and due to heterogeneous sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. The study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models. The authors also note that answer labels for the test set will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visual contexts. It is divided into testmini, intended for model development validation or for those with limited computing resources, and test, intended for standard evaluation. It is used for deterministic evaluation with accuracy as the metric. The paper also positions it as useful for comprehensive qualitative and quantitative evaluation of LLMs and LMMs.
